maria_g: FYI encountered a crash in the sampleapp on Android 14->15 when a multipart upload hits 401 and the client retries. Stack: Unrepeatable request body (stream already consumed). Happens after we upgraded to the coroutine CallAdapter v2 and enabled retryOnConnectionFailure. Repro and logs below.

leo_w: interesting. does the crash happen in the Authenticator path or an Interceptor?

maria_g: root cause looks like this: okhttp's Authenticator triggers a transparent retry with a new Request built from response.request, but our streaming MultipartBody.Part uses a RequestBody that reads InputStream once. When OkHttp tries to replay, it throws. Logs: 

```
E/OkHttp: java.lang.IllegalStateException: request body is not repeatable
    at okhttp3.internal.http.RetryAndFollowUpInterceptor.createRequestWithUpdatedAuth(RetryAndFollowUpInterceptor.java:XXX)
    at okhttp3.internal.http.RetryAndFollowUpInterceptor.intercept(RetryAndFollowUpInterceptor.java:YYY)
    at okhttp3.internal.http.RealInterceptorChain.proceed(RealInterceptorChain.java:ZZZ)
    ...
```

maria_g: Repro steps: 1) start upload large file via sampleapp (streaming request body), 2) server returns 401, 3) Authenticator does blocking refresh, 4) OkHttp tries to replay original request -> crash. Happens reliably on device and emulator when file > ~128KB.

sam_k: this is a classic non-repeatable body + Authenticator retry interaction. Historically people used two approaches: 1) avoid Authenticator and do refresh in Interceptor with single-flight refresh + buffer small bodies, or 2) implement a repeatable/wrapping RequestBody that caches bytes in temp file so it can be replayed. Both have trade-offs (memory/disk).

leo_w: thought: could we make the SDK's example RequestBody use a 'ReplayableRequestBody' that writes to a temp file when size > threshold and replays the stream on demand? That would keep sampleapp robust without pushing users to change Authenticator behavior. Also document the caveat in onboarding: streaming bodies are non-repeatable and will fail with Authenticator retries.

maria_g: I prototyped a small wrapper: 

```
class ReplayableRequestBody(private val source: InputStream, private val thresholdBytes: Int = 256*1024): RequestBody() {
  private val cacheFile: File by lazy { File.createTempFile("reqbuf", null) }
  override fun contentType(): MediaType? = MediaType.parse("application/octet-stream")
  override fun contentLength(): Long = -1L // unknown
  override fun writeTo(sink: BufferedSink) {
    if (!cacheFile.exists()) {
      cacheFile.outputStream().use { out -> source.copyTo(out) }
    }
    cacheFile.inputStream().use { it.copyTo(sink.outputStream()) }
  }
}
```

maria_g: using wrapper, retries no longer crash; OkHttp can replay. Downsides: temp file usage on device and extra I/O for large files. I added cleanup and only buffer if stream > threshold.

sam_k: Another angle: recommend moving the refresh into an Interceptor instead of Authenticator. Interceptor approach can decide not to replay streaming bodies and instead surface 401 to app to do a manual retry with a new upload request. But that shifts complexity to app. For SDK, I like the ReplayableRequestBody helper and a config flag `sdk.upload.bufferLargeStreams=true` with threshold. We can ship helper and note disk usage in docs.

leo_w: +1 for helper in SDK. Also add a unit test in sampleapp that uploads a generated stream > threshold while stubbing 401 and simulating refresh path. Add note for coroutine CallAdapter v2 changes and `retryOnConnectionFailure` interactions.

devex-bot: Created issue RED-DEVEX-3387: "Add ReplayableRequestBody helper + docs for streaming body + Authenticator interactions" and attached prototype. <https://redwood.internal/issue/RED-DEVEX-3387>

maria_g: I'll open a PR with the helper, sampleapp integration, and e2e flakiness test. Will default to off and opt-in via builder. Thanks for the quick triage.

sam_k: Also add a short note in the Android SDK migration guide: "If you stream requests (multipart or InputStream) and rely on OkHttp Authenticator retries, consider buffering or moving refresh into Interceptor."

maria_g: filing PR now :rocket:
